entry.title: Sometimes, You Overcook
entry.summary: I got something cooking. I don't mean that figuratively, at least…
entry.content:
I got something cooking.

I don't mean that figuratively, at least not in this context.

I've got a couple of pots of Korean food going.

So let's keep this shortish.

But I figured, let it boil.

So I can muse.

I got some time to boil away.

So musing it is.

For the record, cooking and musing is a terrible idea.

But what can I say?

I love ideas.

It's the start of the holiday season.

A time, hopefully, for you to slow down.

To stop.

And smell the roses.

Or whatever the fall and winter equivalent is.

Oxtail soup?

My wife says I tend to hibernate in the upcoming seasons.

And I figure that might not be a bad idea.

I could use the rest.

So could she.

How about you?

I turned off one of the pots.

Not much happens from now till the end of the year.

But it seems like this year isn't like most.

I've never wanted time to go faster and slower simultaneously than I do now.

Sorry for being cryptic.

But there are things that only my inner orbis gets to know.

And while you're all in the orbis, you're more outer orbis.

What?

Like you share everything (anything?) with me.

The longer you cook a kimchi jigae, the sweeter and milder it gets.

So long as you keep feeding it water.

And I'm in this weird season where spice is too spicy.

I've gotten up to check on my food a half dozen times since starting this musing.

What a terrible idea.

I hope your holiday season is the excellent equivalent opposite of cooking whilst musing. Musing whilst cooking.

I started writing this thing a little over a year ago.

And it's helped me.

More than I could have imagined.

I encourage you to try it yourself.

Just keep the pots and pans cold until you're done cooking on the laptop.

entry.title: 2026 Is Strange
entry.summary: I'm living in the strangest season of my life. And you've…
entry.content:
I'm living in the strangest season of my life.

And you've had some strange seasons.

I wish I could tell you more, but I don't want to.

You might not believe me, anyway.

There's that old saying, if you are healthy, you have a thousand problems.

When you are not, you have one.

It puts things into proper perspective.

First principles.

Can I breathe?

Do I have a roof over head?

Do I have enough to I eat and drink?

Am I well taken care of?

And to those questions, I answer a resounding "Yes!"

Am I of sound health?

That's the part I'm working on.

With a team of people.

So there's a plan in place.

Has it been a bumpless plan?

No, we're kinda off-roading here.

But it's a plan.

And it's changed.

Because I got rocked.

Is it true everyone has a plan?

I don't think so.

Do you have a plan?

How much fight do you have in you?

Having a plan is all well and good.

Until you get punched in the face.

Then it's about how much fight you got in you.

Like compound interest, all the growth comes at the end.

entry.title: Iterating
entry.summary: What is it that they say about idle hands? Well, it's…
entry.content:
What is it that they say about idle hands?

Well, it's true.

Your hands always find something to do.

And if it ain't productive, well...

It'll play.

I got an honest question for you:

How much of your life is input?

And how much is output?

Meaning, how much of your day is absorbing data?

And how much of it is you producing it?

I admit, too much of my day is consuming.

Not enough compute.

I used to believe that was a point of achievement.

Now, I'm ashamed I ever thought it.

The trick is, such as tricks go, is to figure out what to output.

I don't think it's a time in thing.

The 10,000 hours thing.

I think that thought has changed to 10,000 iterations.

Iterating 10,000 times.

But what do you iterate?

There's a timeline where everyone has enough of their needs met that they're at the top of the hierarchy.

Focusing on building love, potential, and achieving it.

Beyond self.

Some people have it now.

How would you spend your days?

Those 40+ hours given back?

Would your hands do it with all thy might?

Or would they be idle?

Pick something.

Hopefully beneficial to yourself and society.

And work on it.

10,000 times.

Like a game of Telephone, the end will be nothing like the beginning.

But I think, I hope, that's the point.

The point isn't really becoming a "success."

It's whether or not you picked something productive to do with your hands.

And spent a lifetime perfecting it.

entry.summary: Simplicity. Can be easily made complex. Resist the urge. There's usually…
entry.content:
Simplicity.

Can be easily made complex.

Resist the urge.

There's usually a simple answer.

Quite simple.

Stupidly obviously simple.

Don't overcomplicate.

Oversimplify.

Smart move.

entry.title: Tougher Than A Three Dollar Steak
entry.summary: I don't always know what to say here. What to muse…
entry.content:
I don't always know what to say here.

What to muse about.

When I sits.

To say and muse.

 So I'm going to say something to all the men out there.

Without being all gender generalized, I want to say men need to hear this more than women.

Because women tend to do the right thing.

At least in this context.

Fellas, if you can sense something is wrong with your health, get it checked out.

This message is especially for those who believe they are invincible.

You have trusted your gut your entire life.

And if your gut is telling you something isn't right.

Get it checked out.

There are no fields I hate vehemently dislike more than fields where they act as if you work for them, but really you're the ones who are in charge. 

When it comes to your health and wellbeing, you are in charge.

I got a little silly after surviving a big thing that I let myself go, because I was just so thankful to be here.

But like all (soon to be) classic cars, you gotta put in a lot of work to keep it a classic.

Otherwise they throw it in a scrap metal heap.

Oh, and to any stubborn women out there, please trust your gut, too.

I was poked and prodded hundreds of times.

To the point where they couldn't find any veins anymore left to poke.

So I said no more.

And when things got bad, I waited too long to go back to ask for help.

I vehemently dislike to generalize again, but men seem to do that.

I mused (yesterday?) about a hospice doctor who said many of his patients "discovered" at the very end that their life was meant to experience all that life has to offer.

That it was perfect that way.

Maybe holistic is another word we could put on it.

Remember that show Little House on the Prairie?

Well, our family started watching it while I was healing.

I couldn't watch because I realized almost every episode was a sad one.

Most times there'd be a happy ending, with the Ingalls putting on a pot of fresh coffee in the middle of the night.

But I couldn't watch it.

I felt I was living it, to some weird extent.

One of the things I loved about the show was the way they would help others.

Charles would pitch it like it was the other person who was doing him the favor.

"Boy, we sure did make too much soup, we sure would be sad to let any of it spoil."

So listen.

What I'm saying is this.

And I know I'm all over the place but that's just who I am.

Remember Rocky running up those steps?

Iconic.

Pinnacle moment.

But guess what?

He still has to fight the championship fight.

Sometimes, we celebrate the stairs moments a little too much.

We all love goosebump moments and training montages.

When we really need to wrap our hands for the next, real, fight.

And while I can't give you a cufflink from Rocky Marciano, I can give you this:

"Get up, you son of a good woman, 'cause Alex loves you."

How much fight you got left in you, champ?

I know you got a lot.

But even world champions need to rest and heal in between fights.

So heal up.

Until it's time to ring the bell.

Get up.

Until it's time to go.

entry.title: Everything Is Perfect
entry.summary: There's this clip of a doctor who ended up taking care…
entry.content:
There's this clip of a doctor who ended up taking care of hospice patients.

Many come in with so many regrets.

So many failures.

And what he said is that by the end, they all seem to realize that their life was perfect.

That it wasn't meant to just be happy.

It was meant to be all experienced.

Life was meant to be lived.

Now I don't know if this was a real clip or ai generated.

I don't think anyone can know anymore.

But I like this idea.

Not of people passing.

But that when they do, right before they do, they view their life as perfection.

"[At that point,] the victory is no longer staying alive, it's integrating everything that's happened."

"And I got to watch, over and over again, that humans in the last few minutes of life, suddenly look back and realize that their life was perfect."

"And they start feeling an ecstatic moment where they realize, oh my God, the whole thing was poetically perfect. All of the heartbreak. All of the estrangement. All of the disappointment. All of the insecurity. I did that for the experience. And I felt everything. I felt everything a human could feel."

"And they suddenly realized it had nothing to do with any of those [traditional indicators of success] metrics, it had to do with the experience of feeling everything a human being is capable of."

I hope you feel everything a human being is capable of.

And I know now, that it was never meant to be easy.

It was meant to be perfect.

To feel everything a human could feel.

I don't wish any of the negatives of life upon you.

I wish only the positive.

But I'm learning, there is not one without the other.

And I've always had this, not fear, but ignorance of passing.

I avoided it like many young(ish) and old(ish) men do.

Have you felt everything a human being is capable of?

What a poetically perfect question.

And remember, no matter what you're going through, when it's time to say good-bye, you will realize that your life was/is/will be perfection.

Just as it should be.

My loved ones should know, I don't need to be near my good-bye time to understand, to feel, to believe, that my life is perfection.

I know.

Right now.

Because I have felt what a human should feel.

Maybe not everything.

But it's an interesting lens to view the not so good stuff.

👓

And one I hope you find useful.

As it does me.

My Umma used to say "Everything gonna fine." 

In her unique form of English.

She's since added the "be" before fine.

But we like the original phrase best.

My family uses it to this day.

Everything gonna fine.

Amen.

🙏

entry.title: It's All In Your Head
entry.summary: Folks, I have some strange news to share. I no longer…
entry.content:
Folks, I have some strange news to share.

I no longer drink Coke Zero.

Or any caffeine for that matter.

Going cold turkey (weird term) on the Zero hasn't been that difficult.

I'm sure I had withdrawal symptoms but they kinda faded in the background to all my other stuff I was going through.

It's crazy to say, but I don't miss it.

But guess what?

Chicken butt.

I also no longer eat Doritos.

Just went cold chicken on that, too.

Just cold poultrying everything.

It occurred to me that maybe I had all these issues because I was giving myself terrible fuel.

Low gas, no travel.

You know, the kinda fuel so low that you don't find it at most gas stations.

I wish I could tell you I'm a changed man because of the diet change.

And well, I am a changed man, but I'm not sure what has helped that most.

My fingers are no longer coated in a delicious powdered orange. 

My jaw is more relaxed.

And I'm eating food that's more nutritious.

And you know what?

I like drinking water.

We are creatures of routine.

So highly adaptable.

It amazes me that I have Coke Zero and Doritos around and I'm not tempted to eat it.

Not even a little.

Because I feel better without it.

Ain't that something?

Something I did everyday, multiple times a day, almost every meal.

I no longer do.

Just one day, after some considerable nudging, I stopped.

Now, I'm not expecting a standing ovation to stop drinking soda and eating tortilla chips, but I'll give myself one.

Take care of yourselves out there.

We all know that, but I haven't.

Not for a long time.

When I survived, I just thought, I'm just happy to be here.

But that sheet changed.

Changing.

Change.

I'm still absolutely happy to be here.

But I no longer want to act like a guy who is happy he just exists.

I want to act like a person who is happy he exists and takes care of himself to the level that proves he's earned survival.

I don't think Doritos are all that addictive.

Yes, it is.

But I know caffeine sure is.

And I've got it down to just about zero.

I don't think I consume any, but maybe it's somewhere in something.

This is what an old(ish) musings columns gives you.

And I hope you learned something.

You don't put 85 octane in a premium vehicle.

Do you?

I don't know.

But what I'm saying is take care of yourself better than you are.

Changing a habit is doable.

You can give up things you "love" to improve the things that make you love.

And I think you should.

But hey, that's just me musing.

And if I can give up the Ritos and 0, you can too.

Your figurative Ritos and 0.

You get me.

Do it!

I triple dog dare you.

entry.title: Different Old, Different Old
entry.summary: What could I tell you, that hasn't been told a bizillion…
entry.content:
What could I tell you, that hasn't been told a bizillion times before?

...

Much of life is fraught with things you really don't think about until it happens to you or someone close to you.

I say fraught but I could just as easily say blessed.

It doesn't feel like one at the time, but if you can get through it (and I know you can), you will often view it as a learning lesson.

A wissmart moment.

Who wants to be wisdumb?

No, no, the goal is to be wissmart.

Another thing I'll tell you is that everything has a price.

Not always fiat.

But always paid in full.

If not immediately, then later.

I suppose people call it karma.

I sometimes do.

These aren't particularly novel ideas, hmm?

How about this:

If your life was a movie, would you pay to watch it?

Would you spend the hour and forty to sit and see?

What would be in the film?

What would you make up?

I hope you wouldn't make anything up, but they do, you know.

They make a movie about someone who really lived and sometimes make stuff up.

Why?

To make the life more interesting.

Ain't that something?

"Based on a true story."

Means kinda true.

Some parts not so much.

In a good story, there is tension.

Could be internal.

Could be ex.

But it requires the character to change.

It requires what they call an inciting incident.

A usually crazy event that disrupts one's normal routine.

Introducing the conflict.

And the main character then has to make a choice.

He has to take action that differs wildly from his typical activities.

This HAS to happen.

In a good story.

It HAS to.

A story about a guy who hits 500 foot homers every time he steps up to the plate would be a boring story.

It would!

Unless he got bonked on the head and went blind.

And spent five years learning to hit by echo location.

What I'm trying to say is if you're going through it, remember it's part of the story.

And if you haven't gone through it yet, oooh baby, do you got it coming.

But remember:

Every story is a love story.

And every good story has to have a litlle (lot) of chaos.

And as much as I just want to live in peace and just be left alone (with my tribe), I realize that's just a dreamland.

It's time to act.

So, I ask, how's life?

And, more importantly, what are you going to do about it?

Action is expensive.

In costs.

Sweat.

Heartbeats.

Money.

Time.

But the alternative is to ignore it.

To do nothing.

And let me tell you something, that just makes for a greater conflict down the line.

Believe me, I've lived it.

Am living it.

All because I didn't want to act.

Because I felt it was opening Pandora's Box.

But the the truth is, the longer I waited, the bigger the box became.

So open the box, already.

Your life could use a little action.

C'mon, admit it.

Let's get a little crazy and tell a better story.

Your story.

Love.

💛

entry.title: Royal Ramble
entry.summary: So how's everyone doing out there? You good? I'm good enough…
entry.content:
So how's everyone doing out there?

You good?

I'm good enough to type a musing.

Although the quality I'll leave up to you.

Not that this all that, but I'm glad to be writing again.

The body is incredibly adaptable.

Perhaps too much so.

You can learn to live with a lot of crap.

You can learn to live with so much.

It can even begin to feel normal.

What is abnormal is now normal.

I have the distinct advantage of never being normal a day in my life.

So I'm used to this "being different" thing.

You might be, too.

At the end of the night, I'm a motivational speaker.

At least, I'd like to think so.

So I want to tell you what you're going through right now.

Good, bad, everything.

It'll pass.

It's just about getting through it.

My friend used to say "inch by inch."

Like a tortoise.

🐢

But it's really about getting through the next X seconds.

Getting through the next second, minute, hour, day, week.

You get the ⏳.

I hear Einstein said time's an illusion.

Past, present, and future.

Same thing.

Instead of now, there's this 4D cube that has everything that has ever happened and ever will happen.

To me, "science" has always been so much more wildly unbelievable than the idea that there's God.

Sure, it simplifies things.

But I like simple.

I was able to survive something that oofs folks.

But it came and comes with consequences.

I keep and bear them as the cost of survival.

Side effects, they sometimes call them.

But nothing side about them.

They seem main effects to me.

But listen, I don't write a negative musings column.

So I want you to listen.

Listen really close.

Consequence is the finest teacher.

And healing can be instant, but it is often nonlinear.

And yes, you can get used to the suck.

If you have to.

I hope I don't have to for long.

But I have been.

Action -> Consequence.

I learn lessons every day.

God (in his 4D cube) is the greatest teacher.

👑

entry.title: Tilt The Picture, It's A Little Crooked
entry.summary: What's the luckiest moment of your life? You don't have to…
entry.content:
What's the luckiest moment of your life?

You don't have to tell me.

But I'd like you to think about it.

I'm not talking accomplishments.

I'm talking luck.

Something that happens seemingly by pure chance.

Not by skill.

Hard work.

Or strategy.

Just plain old magic.

Do you believe in magic?

I do.

Can you believe in God and magic?

I dunno.

But I do.

What is your luckiest moment?

What are your five luckiest moments?

Ten?

How high can you go?

How lucky have you been?

How lucky are you?

I want to learn to reframe.

Reframing is looking at the same thing from a different perspective.

I'm not (just) an old(ish) curmudgeon.

🖼

I'm lucky to be alive.

You are, too.

You are, too.

For the next day, week, life, act as if you're the luckiest person in the world.

See what happens.

🎲
